newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: YUGOSLAV TREPCA SIGNS $135MLN EXPORT DEAL WITH MYTILINEOS.
newsitem.headline: YUGOSLAV TREPCA SIGNS $135MLN EXPORT DEAL WITH MYTILINEOS.

text.p: The Yugoslav metals giant Trepca of Kosovska Mitrovica and Greek metals trading company Mytilineos have concluded a $135 million export deal, the Belgrade daily Borba reported on Wednesday.

Under the agreement, signed on Tuesday by Trepca general manager Novak Bjelic and Mytilineos chairman Evangelos Mytilineos, Trepca will deliver metals and other products to its Greek partner over a period of two years.
No-one at Trepca was immediately available for comment.

Rudarsko Metalurski Kombinat Trepca, based in Serbia's south province of Kosovo, is the country's largest metals complex employing some 12,000 people. It includes 14 lead and zinc plus metallurgical plants.
The two companies first signed a deal worth $51 million last December, shortly after sanctions against rump Yugoslavia were suspended.

Under that deal Trepca has already delivered $18 million worth of lead and zinc and plans to export another $15 million worth of its products by the end of the year. The balance is to be exported in 1997.
"Without such financial support Trepca would certainly not have been able to restart production and revitalise its installations," Bjelic said.
Trepca plans to raise annual production to $500 million by the year 2000 of which around $300 million would be exported. --Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
